And in the year 627 [1229/1230],
al-Malik al-Ashraf took Baalbek from al-Malik al-Amjad, its lord;
and he entered and dwelt in Damascus in the palace of his father, after he brought out with him everything he found in the treasures of Baalbek.
And in the same year, at its beginning, the Khwarazmshah Jalal al-Din Mangbarni, the son of the Khwarazmshah Muhammad, marched down against Khilat and besieged it,
and waged fierce war against it.
And there were in it both brothers of al-Malik al-Ashraf:
Taqi al-Din Abbas and Mujir al-Din Ya'qub.
For this Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah had at first desired to reign over the land of Sinjar
five years earlier,
and he came to Daquqa and Bawazij (Bayt Waziq,
Kuneshabur?),
and devastated,
and burned,
and put to the sword.
And from there he went to the meadows of Shahrazur;
and Muzaffar al-Din, the lord of Erbil (Arbel?), sent him many gifts,
and made peace with him.
And in this year he came against Khilat,
and set up twenty mangonels against it from the side of the lake.
And the battle and the famine pressed hard upon the people of Khilat,
so much so that they ate the flesh of dogs and donkeys.
And a litra of bread was sold according to the Surḥa weight,
that is, six litras according to the Babylonian weight,
for an Egyptian dinar.
Then Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad assembled a great gathering of twenty thousand,
and came to Melitene;
and he sent ten thousand to the city of Erzincan,
and kept ten thousand with him.
And he sent his maternal uncle {OCR?} to al-Ashraf and said to him
that he himself would go in person to encounter the Khwarazmshah at Khilat.
And: 'If the Lord wills,
I will water his horses from the waters of the Gihon of Persia.'
And he also sent an envoy to the Khwarazmshah and said to him:
'You are a sultan, the son of a sultan,
and it is not fitting that you do anything that is not lawful.
For your father also,
because of his oppression, God stirred up against him the armies of the Tatars from the East.
